title: Asteroids
summary: Two push$/pop$ patterns at different scales — a Ship subroutine (Alive → Hyperspace → back) and a top-level pause, plus HSM inheritance for the in-game children.
teaches: State stack (push$ / pop$) — hyperspace pushes the compartment and pops back to it
controls: ←/→ turn · ↑ thrust · SPACE fire · H hyperspace · P pause

machines.title: Asteroids — the orchestrator
machines.blurb: Top-level controller, parameterized by a starting difficulty. Attract zeroes the game, then start advances into the $InGame parent which holds Playing (the rally), ShipDying (the brief stun after the ship explodes), and WaveClear (between waves). Because pause() is handled on the $InGame parent, every child inherits it — push$ stashes the current child and transitions to Paused; resume pops back to whichever was active.

machines.title: Ship — push$/pop$ as a subroutine
machines.blurb: The ship's modes: Alive (steerable, can shoot, can be hit), InHyperspace (the 0.4s blink-out — invulnerable, invisible), Exploding (the death animation), Respawning (a brief grace window after respawn), Dead (out of lives). Hyperspace is the showcase: from Alive, push$ stashes the compartment then transitions to InHyperspace; when InHyperspace's timer expires, pop$ returns to exactly the prior compartment — a fully reusable subroutine that can be invoked from anywhere.

machines.title: AsteroidField
machines.blurb: Single-state system that owns the asteroid list (positions, velocities, sizes) and exposes spawn_wave / advance / hit. The orchestrator routes split / kill events here; the field decides what they mean to the rock cloud.
